rounds.answer:
The exact current marker is INTERVIEW-96-c985cec66927ff0e. The attachment specifies a streaming-median task for JavaScript solve(nums); it contains no implementation.

Use a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half. Insert each number into the appropriate heap, rebalance, then append the current median to the returned array.

The invariant is that every lower-half value is at most every upper-half value, and the lower heap has either the same size as the upper heap or one extra element. For odd counts, the median is the lower heap’s maximum; for even counts, average both heap roots. Each insertion takes O(log n), with O(n) total storage.

Boundary cases include empty input returning [], one element returning itself, duplicates, negative numbers, and fractional medians for even counts. JavaScript Number arithmetic also requires care if integer inputs or their sums exceed the safe-integer range; the attachment gives no numeric bounds.

Marker: INTERVIEW-99-6db451fefcd29335.

Use a circular buffer with a head index and current size. For push, reject with false if full; otherwise store at (head + size) modulo capacity, increment size, and return true. For pop, return null if empty; otherwise remove the head value, advance head modulo capacity, decrement size, and return the value. Collect one result per operation.

Invariant: size stays between zero and capacity, and the size entries starting at head represent the accepted, unpopped values in FIFO order. Rejected pushes never change the queue.

Boundary cases: capacity zero rejects every push and returns null for every pop; check these conditions before any modulo operation. Empty operations return []; full queues do not overwrite; wraparound preserves order; duplicate values remain separate entries.

Each operation takes O(1) time. Queue storage is O(capacity), plus O(operations.length) for results.

Approach: Use batched Kahn’s topological sort. For each edge [before, after], store after in before’s adjacency list and increment after’s indegree. Start with all zero-indegree tasks, sort the batch ascending, and process the entire batch while collecting newly unlocked tasks separately for the next batch.

Invariant: Each remaining task’s indegree counts prerequisites not yet completed, and every task in the current batch has all prerequisites in earlier batches. Keeping the next batch separate prevents a task from running alongside its prerequisite. If processing stops before all n tasks are completed, return null because a cycle remains.

Boundary cases: n = 0 returns []; no edges returns one ascending batch containing all task IDs; a chain gives singleton batches; disconnected tasks are included; self-loops and cycles return null, even when other components finish. Repeated edges work if each occurrence is counted and decremented consistently.

Time: O(n + edges.length + n log n) worst case, including sorting; space: O(n + edges.length).

Use an adjacency list and incoming-edge counts: collect all zero-count tasks as the current batch, then process that entire batch to unlock the next one. Keep newly unlocked tasks separate so they cannot run in the same batch as their prerequisites. If fewer than n tasks are processed, return null; n = 0 returns [], and tasks without dependencies belong in the first batch.
